definition: Assiduous means showing persistent care and hard work.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word assiduous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know assiduous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The museum's assiduous registrar numbered and photographed all twelve thousand artifacts, never letting a single crate go unlogged.
An attentive clerk notices what is in front of her; assiduous adds persistence - checking and rechecking, day after day, until nothing slips.

Obsessive pushes past assiduous into unhealthy territory: the assiduous bookkeeper double-checks the ledger and goes home, while the obsessive one is still re-adding columns at midnight that already balance.

Industrious praises someone who works hard and stays busy - plenty of hours, plenty of output. Assiduous narrows the praise: not just hard work but persistent, careful attention, so that nothing slips through. You can be industrious and still miss details; the assiduous worker never lets them slip.

Thorough means complete and careful on a single task - every corner checked before the job is called done. Assiduous stretches that care across time, tending the details day after day. One well-finished report is thorough; a decade of them, none ever skipped, is assiduous.

Meticulous care is about precision in the moment - every measurement exact, every detail checked twice. Assiduous care adds time: the same watchful effort kept up day after day, month after month. A meticulous editor perfects one manuscript; an assiduous one guards every issue, year after year.

Assiduous means showing persistent care and hard work.
Marco, an assiduous apprentice electrician, traced every circuit twice, kept a notebook of every fault he had ever seen, and re-checked his own finished work before the inspector could.
By his third year, journeymen were phoning him with questions.
Assiduous goes beyond 'hardworking': it names care that never lets up - steady, watchful attention to every detail, day after day.
A hardworking person puts in the hours; an assiduous one also makes sure nothing slips through them.
Assiduous praises steady, careful effort applied over time - the register is admiring and slightly formal.

Its unit-mates pull in other directions: resolute is about an unshakable decision, and zealous about burning enthusiasm; assiduous is quieter, the virtue of someone who simply never stops tending the details.
In casual speech, 'hardworking' or 'careful' is the plainer choice.

Most beekeepers inspect their hives when trouble appears.
Aurelio Pinto inspects his on a calendar.
Every Sunday for twenty-two years, he has opened all forty hives, weighed each frame, and noted the queen's condition in a canvas notebook -- mites counted, moods recorded, no week skipped.
The assiduous routine looked excessive to his neighbors until the collapse of 2019, when mites swept the valley.
Because his notebook showed exactly when each hive's counts had begun to creep, Pinto treated early and lost two colonies.
The valley's other keepers lost half of theirs.
Inspectors now photocopy his pages for training courses -- twenty-two years of Sundays, they point out, with not one gap in the record.
